name: Medium-voltage switchgear and busway in the data hall
applications: MV distribution from site substations to data hall UPS and PDU plant
Overhead power distribution to rows and racks
principle: MV switchgear is the switching and protection layer between the site transformers and the data hall; busway replaces fixed cable runs with a tap-off busbar so power can be taken off anywhere along a row and racks added without re-cabling. Busway matters at AI densities because the tap-off positions, not the cable schedule, define where a rack can go.

process_steps.name: MV feed enters the data hall switchgear
UPS and PDU plant condition and distribute the load
Overhead busway carries power along the row
Rack PDUs take power at the tap-off point

key_equipment: MV switchgear and ring main units (1-52 kV IEC class)
busway with tap-off units and metering

advantages: Tap-off positions let racks move as density changes
Metering per tap-off makes row-level energy visible
limitations: Busway fault levels and coordination need the whole train modelled
Overhead busway constrains ceiling space and sprinkler layout
MV switchgear lead times are long and SF6 alternatives carry different footprints
